exact_statement: Let g be any Boolean sign on r>=0 uniform bits. Append q>=4 dummy bits and flip its value at one vertex, forming F_q on n=r+q bits; set d=2^(1-n), K=|supp(ghat)|. Every previously irrelevant coordinate becomes relevant with influence d, has the same signed packet multiset u_T=c_T/(g(v)d), and has ratios lambda/d=1+d sum_occupied[ell(u)-1], B/d=2+d sum_occupied[beta(u)-2], D/d=4+d sum_occupied[gamma(u)-4], with kernels specified in PADDING_EDIT_PROOF.md. These satisfy 1<=lambda/d<=1+2Kd(n+1), 2<=B/d<=2+Kd(2n+4), 4<=D/d<=4+Kd(2n+7). For every old relevant coordinate the three ratios converge to their original values as q tends to infinity. Thus the minimum relevant-coordinate ratios converge respectively to min(1,min_old lambda/d), min(2,min_old B/d), min(4,min_old D/d), with empty old minimum +infinity. The dimension-free local continuity bound is |lambda_i(f)-lambda_i(g)|<=h2(epsilon)+epsilon, |B_i(f)-B_i(g)|<=h2(epsilon)+epsilon, |D_i(f)-D_i(g)|<=2[h2(epsilon)+epsilon] when the output edit probability is delta and epsilon=2sqrt(delta)<=1/2. F_q has full Fourier support; for I(g)>0 its H/I tends to H(g)/I(g). Revealing all q appended coordinates spends exactly qd influence and leaves terminal entropy (1-2^-q)H(g)+2^-q H(g^v), and the analogous terminal influence, where g^v is the old core with one flipped vertex.
